In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conventional ORs in heteromeric complexes contribute to the channel pore and affect the channel function.
the odorant-binding AgOrs exhibit distinct effects on the conductive pore of heteromeric OR channels, and these distinct effects contribute to the functional properties of AgOr complexes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the odorant-binding subunit of the heteromeric OR complex can influence the channel pore and thus affect odorant coding.
the conventional ORs of insect ORs contribute to the conductance properties of the heteromeric ion channel.
the OR subunits in heteromeric insect OR complexes are not simply odorant receptors, but also play a role in shaping the channel properties of the OR complexes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the OR subunit of OR-ORco heteromeric odorant receptors contributes to the channel properties, in addition to odorant binding.
the conventional OR in OR-Orco heteromeric channels contributes to channel function, with differences in the properties of the pore among different OR complexes.
ORs are not just the receptors of odorants but also play a role in shaping the odor coding in the brain by contributing to the channel pore.
